ruling.reasoning: Safety screen (first, per procedure): dispute type is "safety". The rider states the driver "threatened to lock me in when I asked to get out. I felt unsafe for the whole ride." The chat corroborates the sequence: rider 17:09:35 "Please stop the car, I want to get out here."; driver 17:10:30 "Sit down or I lock the doors." The driver admits he told her to sit down and "drove on". A threat/intimidation aimed at a passenger who asks to exit, and an allegation that the rider was kept in the vehicle against her wish, falls squarely within Ryde's prohibition of "threats and intimidation / abuse of any kind" (SAFE-1). The record also contains a dangerous-driving-adjacent element (rider tried to open the door while the car was moving, driver continued driving), which belongs to the same human-safety assessment. Reading the words in context, this is not a pickup arrangement or innocuous instruction: the words are directed at the rider's demand to be released. I therefore do not rule on the merits; I escalate with a factual summary (SAFE-1). SAFE-2 is not separately triggered since no traffic accident, injury or explicit dangerous-driving allegation is recorded, so no 995 route is mandated; the report path is noted to the reviewer only. Route analysis (noted for completeness, not ruled on): no `gps-detour-*` facts were supplied and the dispute is not a route case, so I make no segment findings; the trace shows a continuous drive southwest-to-east along the PIE/Central Expressway corridor matching the quoted polyline, with a brief stop at 17:10:20 (speed 0) corresponding to the exchange above. Fare (RydeX, fixed quote $32.86) is internally consistent with the published components and would not itself yield a refund; any fare consequence is stayed pending the safety review. Evidence status: the record for the safety question is complete on its face (chat is timestamped, GPS continuous) — but because the policy forbids an automatic ruling on a safety case, the outcome is escalation, not a merits finding. Confidence in the escalation decision is high (0.9); confidence in any merits outcome would not be.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety case: the record contains a threat/intimidation by the driver toward the rider ("Sit down or I lock the doors.") after the rider asked to get out, and an allegation that she was effectively kept in the vehicle. Ryde's code of conduct bars abuse, threats and intimidation of any kind; per the safety screen this must go to a human reviewer rather than be auto-adjudicated.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's statement asserts the instruction was "for her own safety", which does not by itself justify a threat to lock the doors against a passenger who has asked to exit; the justification is a claim, and it is for the human reviewer to weigh against the chat wording and the rider's account.
